name: Jagannath Temple, Chennai
significance: A modern shrine at Kannathur off the East Coast Road south of Chennai, built in Kalinga style for the divine trinity of Jagannath, Baladeva and Subhadra. It was consecrated on 26 January 2001 and serves the city's Odia community.

name: Ardhagiri
significance: A hill shrine to Hanuman at Aragonda in Chittoor district, Andhra Pradesh, whose name means 'half mountain'. It is known for a perennial spring on the hill that pilgrims regard as medicinal.
story: Legend holds that when Hanuman was carrying the Dronagiri mountain of healing herbs, Bharata shot him down with an arrow and half the mountain fell here, giving the place its name.

name: Ghaghar Burhi Temple
deity: Kali, worshipped as Ghaghar Buri Chandi Mata
significance: A shrine of the goddess Kali on the bank of the Damodar near Asansol in Paschim Bardhaman district, West Bengal. It is one of the most visited local pilgrimage spots of the Asansol industrial belt.
story: Local tradition tells of a wedding party trapped by a flooded rivulet who prayed to the goddess and crossed safely, but the king forgot his vow of a sacrifice and the party was cursed to remain beneath the water.

name: Chakra Narasimha Temple
significance: A Vaishnava shrine near the seashore at Chakratirtha in Puri, Odisha, where forms of Narasimha are worshipped alongside a large granite wheel venerated as the Sudarshana Chakra. It is counted among the tirthas of the Puri pilgrimage circuit and also serves as a shrine to Varuna.
story: The site is said to mark the spot where the sacred wood for the first images of Jagannath, Balabhadra, Subhadra and Sudarshana came ashore after floating in the sea for Indradyumna.

name: Olakkannesvara Temple
significance: A stone temple to Shiva perched on the rock above the Mahishasuramardini cave at Mahabalipuram, raised under the Pallava king Rajasimha in the early 8th century. Its walls carry panels of Shiva as Kalantaka, Dakshinamurti, Nataraja and in the Ravananugraha episode.

name: Krishna Mandapam
significance: A rock-cut relief panel at Mahabalipuram carved in the mid-7th century under the Pallavas, showing Krishna raising Govardhana amid scenes of cowherd village life. A pillared mandapa was built in front of it in the 16th century under the Vijayanagara empire.
story: The relief depicts Krishna lifting the Govardhana hill on one finger to shelter the cowherds from the deluge sent by Indra.

name: Ganesha Temple, Idagunji
significance: A much-visited Ganesha shrine at Idagunji in Uttara Kannada district, Karnataka, near Honnavara, traced in the article to the 4th–5th century CE. The two-armed standing image is unusual and draws large numbers of pilgrims each year.
story: It is said that the sage Valakhilya, obstructed in a sacrifice on the Sharavathi bank, was advised by Narada to worship Ganesha, who agreed to remain at Kunjavana, the grove that became Idagunji.

name: Sani Monastery
significance: A Drukpa Kagyu monastery in the Zanskar valley of Ladakh, a few kilometres from Padum, whose foundation is traditionally carried back to the Kushan emperor Kanishka. It is unusual among Zanskar gompas in standing on flat ground rather than a crag, and encloses the ancient Kanika stupa.
story: Padmasambhava is said to have spent five years in a small chapel at the site, and the monastery is also linked in tradition to the yogi Naropa and to the epic king Gesar.

name: Devipuram
deity: Sahasrakshi, a form of Lalita Tripurasundari, with Kameshwara
significance: A Shakta temple complex in Anakapalli district, Andhra Pradesh, founded by the nuclear physicist N. Prahalada Sastry, whose Sahasrakshi Meru shrine is built as a three-dimensional Sri Meru Yantra. Construction ran from 1985 to consecration in 1994.
story: Its founder described a meditative vision of himself lying on the peetam while four figures performed a homa with flames rising from his body, after which a panchaloha Sri Chakra Maha Meru was found at the site.

name: Jagannath Temple, Hyderabad
significance: A temple on Road 12, Banjara Hills, built in 2009 by Hyderabad's Odia community and run by the Kalinga Cultural Trust. Its design follows the Jagannath temple at Puri, with a shikhara of about seventy feet.

name: Banashankari Temple, Amargol
significance: An early 13th-century stone temple at Amargol between Hubli and Dharwad, notable for pairing a nagara shrine of stepped-diamond plan with a dravida one. It stands beside the Shankarlinga temple and is a protected monument under the Archaeological Survey of India.

name: Ananthagiri Temple
significance: A hill temple to Vishnu in the Ananthagiri forest of Vikarabad district, Telangana, dated by the article to roughly four centuries ago and endowed by the Nizams, with the seventh Nizam Mir Osman Ali Khan funding work there. The hills around it are the source of the Musi river.
story: Tradition says the deity appeared to a Nizam in a dream asking that a temple be raised, and earlier that the sage Markandeya installed the image here and had the Ganga brought for his bathing.
